questions.q: Why can't you "call the blockchain" the way you'd call a single server?
options: Ethereum is thousands of independently run nodes, so talking to the chain always means talking to one specific node's RPC endpoint
Blockchains don't accept any network requests at all
There is exactly one official Ethereum server, but it's permanently offline
JSON-RPC was deprecated and replaced by a single global API
questions.explain: There's no single chain-wide server — every request goes to one particular node, chosen by whichever RPC endpoint you configure.

questions.q: What protocol does an Ethereum node use to answer requests like "what's this wallet's balance"?
options: JSON-RPC
GraphQL exclusively
FTP
SMTP
questions.explain: Every Ethereum node speaks JSON-RPC — methods like eth_getBalance and eth_call — regardless of which provider runs it.

questions.q: Why do most teams pay a node provider like Infura or Alchemy instead of running their own node?
options: Running a full node means hundreds of gigabytes of storage, hours of sync time, and a server you must keep online and patched forever
Running your own node is illegal in most countries
Self-hosted nodes cannot process JSON-RPC requests
Node providers are required by the Ethereum protocol itself
questions.explain: Self-hosting is real, ongoing infrastructure work; a managed provider trades that for an API key and a monthly bill.

questions.q: What does an RPC endpoint URL like https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR-API-KEY actually represent?
options: The address your code sends JSON-RPC requests to, with your provider API key embedded in the path
A download link for the full Ethereum blockchain
A wallet address that holds your account's ETH
The URL of a block explorer page
questions.explain: It's the HTTP address a library like ethers.js or viem sends JSON-RPC requests to — the key in the path authenticates and meters your usage.

questions.q: What is chainlist.org, as used in this lesson?
options: A live, community-maintained directory of public RPC endpoints per chain, with real-time latency and block height
A paid node provider competing with Infura and Alchemy
The official Ethereum Foundation's only approved RPC list
A tool for deploying smart contracts
questions.explain: Chainlist is a discovery tool for comparing real public RPC endpoints — it doesn't run nodes itself, it lists ones others run.
